knowledge:
- key_parameters: method="noether" ;; na.rm=TRUE ;; time.cens=tc/365 ;; q=0.05 ;; list.cindex1=listOne ;; list.cindex2=listTwo
- alternatives: None mentioned as direct replacements, but the package depends on survival, ipred, prodlim, survivalROC, SuppDists, and bootstrap.
- when_to_use: When evaluating risk prediction models on survival data, especially when integrating results across multiple independent transcriptomic datasets using meta-analysis.
- pitfalls: Microarray platforms (e.g., Affymetrix vs. Agilent) have different gene expression ranges, which directly affects hazard ratio computation. Gene expression data must be rescaled (e.g., using a robust quantile-based rescaling function) before computing hazard ratios to ensure comparability. Censoring times may differ across datasets; artificial censoring using censor.time is recommended to align them.

workflows.name: survival_risk_prediction_evaluation
workflows.intent: Compute concordance index, D-index, and hazard ratio for risk predictors across multiple datasets, combine the estimates, and visualize them using forest plots.
input: ExpressionSet objects or expression matrices (e.g., mainz7g) and clinical survival data (survival times and events).
workflows.stages: 1. Compute concordance index using concordance.index ;; 2. Compute D-index using D.index ;; 3. Rescale expression data using a custom quantile-based function ;; 4. Compute hazard ratio using hazard.ratio ;; 5. Combine estimates across datasets using combine.est ;; 6. Plot combined estimates using forestplot.surv
workflows.code:
cindexall.mainz.small <- t(apply(X=exprs(mainz7g), MARGIN=1, function(x, y, z) { tt <- concordance.index(x=x, surv.time=y, surv.event=z, method="noether", na.rm=TRUE); return(c("cindex"=tt$c.index, "cindex.se"=tt$se, "lower"=tt$lower, "upper"=tt$upper)); }, y=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"], z=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"]))
dindexall.mainz.small <- t(apply(X=exprs(mainz7g), MARGIN=1, function(x, y, z) { tt <- D.index(x=x, surv.time=y, surv.event=z, na.rm=TRUE); return(c("dindex"=tt$d.index, "dindex.se"=tt$se, "lower"=tt$lower, "upper"=tt$upper)); }, y=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"], z=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"]))
rescale <- function(x, na.rm=FALSE, q=0.05) { ma <- quantile(x, probs=1-(q/2), na.rm=na.rm); mi <- quantile(x, probs=q/2, na.rm=na.rm); x <- (x - mi) / (ma - mi); return((x - 0.5) * 2); }
hratio.mainz.small <- t(apply(X=rescale(exprs(mainz7g) , q=0.05, na.rm=TRUE), MARGIN=1, function(x, y, z) { tt <- hazard.ratio(x=x, surv.time=y, surv.event=z, na.rm=TRUE); return(c("hratio"=tt$hazard.ratio, "hratio.se"=tt$se, "lower"=tt$lower, "upper"=tt$upper)); }, y=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"], z=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"]))
combine.est(x=cbind(cindexall.mainz.small[i,"cindex"], cindexall.transbig.small[i,"cindex"]), x.se=cbind(cindexall.mainz.small[i,"cindex.se"], cindexall.transbig.small[i,"cindex.se"]), na.rm=TRUE)
forestplot.surv(labeltext=labeltext, mean=r.mean, lower=r.lower, upper=r.upper, zero=0.5, align=c("l"), graphwidth=grid::unit(2, "inches"), x.ticks=seq(0.4,0.7,0.05), xlab=paste( "Concordance Index", myspace, sep=""), col=meta.colors(box="royalblue", line="darkblue", zero="darkred"), box.size=bs, clip=c(0.4,1))

workflows.name: survival_curve_visualization
workflows.intent: Plot Kaplan-Meier survival curves for multiple datasets or stratified risk groups with risk tables.
input: Survival times, survival events, and group indicators (e.g., dataset names or stratified gene expression levels).
workflows.stages: 1. Artificially censor survival data using censor.time ;; 2. Create a data frame with time, event, and group ;; 3. Plot Kaplan-Meier curves using km.coxph.plot
workflows.code:
surv.data <- censor.time(surv.time=c(pData(mainz7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"], pData(transbig7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"]) / 365, surv.event=c(pData(mainz7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"], pData(transbig7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"]), time.cens=tc / 365)
gg <- factor(c(rep("mainz", nrow(pData(mainz7g))), rep("transbig", nrow(pData(transbig7g)))), levels=c("mainz", "transbig"))
dd <- data.frame("time"=surv.data[[1]], "event"=surv.data[[2]], "group"=gg)
km.coxph.plot(formula.s=formula(Surv(time, event) ~ group), data.s=dd, sub.s="all", x.label="Time (years)", y.label = "Probability of DMFS/RFS", main.title="", sub.title="", leg.pos="bottomright", leg.inset=0.05, o.text=FALSE, v.line=FALSE, h.line=FALSE, .lty=rep(1, length(levels(gg))), show.n.risk=TRUE, n.risk.step=1, n.risk.cex=0.85, .col=c("darkorange", "red"), leg.text=paste(levels(gg), myspace, sep=""), verbose=FALSE, ylim=c(0.1,1))

workflows.name: performance_comparison_meta_analysis
workflows.intent: Statistically compare the concordance indices of different risk predictors across multiple datasets using meta-analysis.
input: Concordance index objects computed for multiple genes across multiple datasets.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute concordance index objects for each gene in each dataset using concordance.index ;; 2. Construct lists of concordance index objects for the two predictors to be compared ;; 3. Compare the lists of concordance indices across datasets using cindex.comp.meta
workflows.code:
cindexMetaMainz <- t(apply(X=exprs(mainz7g), MARGIN=1, function(x, y, z) { tt <- concordance.index(x=x, surv.time=y, surv.event=z, method="noether", na.rm=TRUE); return(tt); }, y=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"t.dmfs"], z=pData(mainz7g)[ ,"e.dmfs"]))
listOne <- list("mainz" = cindexMetaMainz[[i]], "transbig" = cindexMetaTransbig[[i]])
listTwo <- list("mainz" = cindexMetaMainz[[j]], "transbig" = cindexMetaTransbig[[j]])
rr <- cindex.comp.meta(list.cindex1=listOne, list.cindex2=listTwo)
